reasons: Code is correct and tested; one inaccurate explanatory sentence.

issues.claim: forgetting the re-raise in a @contextmanager makes the generator finish without raising, which can turn a with-body failure into a RuntimeError or silent success
issues.problem: If the generator catches and finishes normally, contextmanager.__exit__ gets StopIteration and returns True, i.e. the exception is silently suppressed. RuntimeError ("generator didn't stop after throw()") only occurs if the generator yields again. Verified from CPython contextlib behaviour.
issues.replacement: forgetting the re-raise in a @contextmanager makes the generator finish normally, so the with statement silently suppresses the body's exception (a RuntimeError appears only if the generator yields a second time)

issues.claim: The broadcast form is exact and simplest for small inputs
issues.problem: Floating-point subtraction/sum is not 'exact'; it is just numerically well-conditioned compared with the expansion.
issues.replacement: The broadcast form is numerically accurate (no cancellation between large norms) and simplest for small inputs

issues.claim: the broadcast version materialises an (n, m, d) temporary, e.g. 5,000 x 5,000 x 128 float64 is about 25.6 GB
issues.problem: 25.6 GB is correct per array but diff**2 creates a second same-size temporary, so peak is roughly double.
issues.replacement: the broadcast version materialises an (n, m, d) temporary (and diff ** 2 a second one), e.g. 5,000 x 5,000 x 128 float64 is about 25.6 GB each

reasons: Answer omits the requested counting wrapper and its results (only present in the test); an O(1)-space claim is wrong for CPython sorting.

issues.claim: Prove the complexity claim ... write a wrapper class that counts __eq__ calls (question) / answer text has no counting class or numbers
issues.problem: The question asks to write the counting wrapper and show the counts; the answer text and fenced code never include it (only the hidden test does).

issues.claim: when memory is tight (an in-place sort of data you may reorder needs O(1) extra space versus the set's O(n))
issues.problem: CPython's list.sort (Timsort) may allocate up to ~n/2 temporary slots, so it is not O(1) extra space; and the shown has_duplicates_sorted uses sorted(), which copies (O(n)).
issues.replacement: when memory is tight and you may reorder the data (list.sort() in place avoids the set and the copy that sorted() makes, though CPython's Timsort can still use up to about n/2 temporary slots, so this saves a constant factor rather than reaching O(1) extra space)

issues.problem: Versions disagree on NaN: for one shared nan object, quadratic -> False, sorted -> False, but has_duplicates -> True (set uses identity before ==). Worth one sentence on 'equal by ==' vs identity.
issues.replacement: Caveat: the set version first checks identity, so the same float('nan') object counted twice is reported as a duplicate even though nan != nan; the quadratic and sorted versions say False.

reasons: Regex uses \d, which matches non-ASCII Unicode digits, violating the stated 'YYYY-MM-DD' and 'digits only' rules.

issues.problem: In Python 3 str patterns \d matches any Unicode decimal digit: 'k=٣' is parsed as int 3 and a timestamp '٢٠٢٦-03-01T12:00:05Z' is accepted (both verified), contradicting 'digits only' and 'YYYY-MM-DD...'. Fix in answer text AND code.solution (tests still pass).
\s also matches \x0b, \x0c and U+2028 etc., so 'a="x"\u2028b=1' parses as two pairs although the spec says space-separated. Acceptable but undocumented.
With ensure_ascii=False a U+2028 in a value stays raw and str.splitlines() would split the line (verified); split('\n') is safe. Consider ensure_ascii=True or note it.
Timestamp ranges are not validated ('2026-13-45T99:99:99Z' accepted) - consistent with 'ISO-like' but should be stated; unknown escapes like \n are kept literally.

difficulty_rationale: Many interacting rules, whole-line validation vs finditer, escape handling, malformed accounting.
code_findings: Extra edges run: empty value k= malformed; k="" ok; leading zeros 007->7, -0->0, +5 and 1_0 stay str; unterminated/odd escape "x\" malformed; a=b"c malformed; lowercase level malformed; tabs as separators accepted; 20k-backslash line returns quickly (no catastrophic backtracking); non-str element raises AttributeError (not specified). Unicode-digit bug confirmed on 3.10 and 3.13. Re-ran solution+test from scratch: passes on Python 3.13 (sandbox), 3.10.20 and 3.11.17 venvs (xrun.py, 12/12 ok); fenced block in answer is byte-identical to code.solution.
